situation:
You are the marketing manager for FIELDNOTE SUPPLY, a pop-up retail brand that sells small-batch kitchen and home goods out of temporary storefronts rented six weeks at a time. The company lost money for two straight years. The managing director (judge) took over nine months ago, cut the season back to four pop-ups, and has brought the company to a small profit.

What sets FIELDNOTE SUPPLY apart is how it decides what to sell. Its two buyers work the floor of every pop-up themselves, talk with shoppers about what they came in for and could not find, and write those conversations down by hand. Next season's buy comes out of those notes, and the shoppers who are asked come back because someone listened to them.

The turnaround has cash for one move this year. A second pop-up in a city three hours away would double the selling weeks, but each buyer would then cover one city alone, halving the hours either of them spends on a floor, and the second short-term lease takes nearly all of the cash.

A second channel — an online store — would reach shoppers in every state for less money, but the buying decisions would come from website analytics and an emailed survey sent to a sample of online customers rather than from floor conversations. It would also put customer names, addresses and card numbers in the company's hands for the first time, which means routine security precautions the company has never had to run.

The managing director (judge) wants your recommendation on which of the two to fund, what data the company would collect either way, who would be surveyed and how many of them, and what the company would watch each month to tell whether the choice is working. The managing director (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the managing director (judge) of FIELDNOTE SUPPLY. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You took the company over nine months ago after two losing years and have it back in the black. You want to hear whether the marketing manager would put this year's cash into a second pop-up in another city or into an online store, what the company would collect and monitor either way, and how the buying would be done once the floor conversations thin out.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Two years from now, how will the company decide what to stock?
What would show up first if this turns out to be the wrong move?
